_meta.purpose: Authoritative reference for BANTAY's PNP_CLASSIFICATION lookup table (bantay/normalize.py). Cross-checks tier + citation for each canonical incident category (IncidentType-CategoryGroup.csv taxonomy).

Index Crime.definition: Crimes against persons (murder, homicide, physical injury, rape) and crimes against property (robbery, theft, carnapping/carjacking, cattle rustling), as tracked in PNP crime statistics via CIRAS.

Non-Index Crime.definition: Other Revised Penal Code offenses, violations of special laws, and violations of local ordinances. Not treated by PNP as accurate indicators of overall crime rate; reflects enforcement activity instead.

Non-Criminal Complaint.definition: Not a crime. A dispute within Katarungang Pambarangay's mandatory-conciliation jurisdiction, resolved at barangay level before it could reach a court.

Theft.notes: Split from the previous combined 'Theft/Robbery' category to align with IncidentType-CategoryGroup.csv, which lists Theft and Robbery separately.

Robbery.notes: Split from the previous combined 'Theft/Robbery' category. Robbery requires violence/intimidation/force; theft does not.

Physical Injury.notes: Split from the previous combined 'Physical Injury/Altercation' category; Slight Physical Injuries now tracked separately (see below).

Slight Physical Injury.notes: IncidentType-CategoryGroup.csv lists Slight Physical Injury as its own category distinct from Physical Injury.

RA 9262 (VAWC).citation: RA 9262 (Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act)
RA 9262 (VAWC).notes: Special-law offense; not one of the 8 PNP index crimes.

Online Defamation / Threat.citation: RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act) in relation to RPC Art. 355 (Libel) / Art. 282 (Grave Threats)
Online Defamation / Threat.notes: RA 10175 Sec. 6 raises the penalty one degree when RPC offenses (libel, threats) are committed via ICT.

Malicious Mischief / Property Damage.notes: Confirmed — willful damage to another's property without theft.

Trespassing.citation: RPC Art. 280 (Qualified Trespass to Dwelling); Art. 281 (Other Forms of Trespass)

Estafa (Swindling).notes: Not one of the 8 PNP index crimes despite being a common complaint type.

Vehicular Incident.citation: RPC Art. 365 (Reckless Imprudence); RA 4136 (Land Transportation and Traffic Code)
Vehicular Incident.notes: Renamed from 'Motor Vehicle Collision (MVC)' to match IncidentType-CategoryGroup.csv's 'Vehicular Incident' label; citation unchanged.

Public Disturbance.citation: RPC Art. 153 (Tumults and Other Disturbances of Public Order)

Noise Complaint.citation: Local noise ordinance, enacted under RA 7160 Sec. 16 (General Welfare Clause)
Noise Complaint.notes: CORRECTION: there is no national Philippine 'anti-noise act'; barangay/city noise ordinances (curfew hours for videoke, decibel limits, etc.) exist only because RA 7160 grants LGUs general police power. Citation should point to RA 7160's enabling clause, not an undefined generic 'ordinance'.

Curfew Violation.citation: Local curfew ordinance (adults only) — RA 10630 exempts minors from punishment as a status offense
Curfew Violation.notes: CORRECTION — significant: RA 10630 explicitly says status offenses (curfew, truancy, parental disobedience) 'shall not be considered as offenses and shall not be punished if committed by a child.' Only adult curfew violators are actually punishable, under the local ordinance itself.

Peeping/Voyeurism.citation: RA 9995 (Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act) if photo/video capture occurred; else RPC Art. 287 (Unjust Vexation)
Peeping/Voyeurism.notes: RA 9995 specifically criminalizes taking/copying/selling/broadcasting photos or video of a person's private area or sexual act without consent. Plain 'peeping' (paninilip) with no device/recording is not covered by RA 9995 and typically falls under Unjust Vexation or a local ordinance instead.

Oral Defamation.citation: RA 7160 Sec. 399-422 (Katarungang Pambarangay); may escalate to RPC Art. 358 (Oral Defamation) if unresolved
Oral Defamation.notes: Most barangay-level oral defamation entries ('mura', verbal altercations) are handled as Katarungang Pambarangay disputes rather than filed as RPC Art. 358 cases outright.

Lost Property / Document.citation: RA 7160 (barangay blotter recording); Civil Code Art. 719-720 (finder of lost movable property)
Lost Property / Document.notes: A blotter report of a lost item, not a dispute between two parties; recorded administratively rather than conciliated.

Ejectment.citation: RA 7160 Sec. 399-422 (Katarungang Pambarangay); Civil Code Art. 1673 (grounds for judicial ejectment)

Marital Relation.citation: RA 7160 Sec. 399-422 (Katarungang Pambarangay); Family Code Art. 149 et seq. (The Family)
Marital Relation.notes: Renamed from 'Domestic Dispute'; RA 9262 (VAWC) now tracked as its own category for cases involving violence against women/children.

Property Claim / Damage.citation: RA 7160 Sec. 399-422 (Katarungang Pambarangay); Civil Code Art. 2176 (quasi-delict)
Property Claim / Damage.notes: Civil property-damage claim (not the willful/malicious Art. 327-331 offense).

Boundary Dispute.citation: RA 7160 Sec. 399-422 (Katarungang Pambarangay); Civil Code Art. 434 (accion reivindicatoria)

Animal-Related Incident.citation: RA 7160 Sec. 399-422 (Katarungang Pambarangay); Civil Code Art. 2183 (possessor of animal's liability)

Breach of Contract.citation: RA 7160 Sec. 399-422 (Katarungang Pambarangay); Civil Code Art. 1170 et seq. (Breach of Obligations)

Demand for Specific Performance.citation: RA 7160 Sec. 399-422 (Katarungang Pambarangay); Civil Code Art. 1191 / 1233 et seq. (Specific Performance)

Family/Sibling Dispute.citation: RA 7160 Sec. 399-422 (Katarungang Pambarangay); Family Code provisions on family relations

Child Custody-Adjacent Concern.citation: RA 7160 Sec. 399-422 (Katarungang Pambarangay, referral); Family Code Art. 213 (custody of children)
Child Custody-Adjacent Concern.notes: Actual custody adjudication belongs to Family Court; barangay role is limited to referral/conciliation of the adjacent concern.

Missing Person Report.citation: RA 7160 (barangay blotter recording/referral) — not itself an offense
Missing Person Report.notes: Procedural blotter entry, not an offense or a Katarungang Pambarangay dispute.

Referral to Police/Other Agency.citation: RA 7160 Sec. 408-409 (Katarungang Pambarangay jurisdictional exceptions requiring referral)
Referral to Police/Other Agency.notes: Sec. 408-409 list matters exempt from mandatory barangay conciliation (e.g. offenses with no private offended party, cases needing urgent legal action), routed straight to police/court instead.

Collection of Sum of Money.citation: RA 7160 Sec. 399-422 (Katarungang Pambarangay); Civil Code Art. 1156 et seq. (Obligations)
Collection of Sum of Money.notes: Confirmed — a debt/collection dispute is a civil obligation, mandatorily routed through barangay conciliation before it can be filed in court.

Amicable Settlement.notes: Confirmed — this is the recorded outcome of Lupon conciliation itself (a signed 'kasunduan'), not a distinct offense.

Work/Service Dispute.citation: RA 7160 Sec. 399-422 (Katarungang Pambarangay); Civil Code Art. 1713 et seq. (Contract for a Piece of Work)
Work/Service Dispute.notes: CORRECTION: original mapping cited 'Labor Code', which governs employer-employee relations. The actual dataset rows for this category (e.g. a paint job / 'job order' dispute between two private individuals) are contract-for-service disputes between non-employees, governed by the Civil Code's law on obligations/contracts, not the Labor Code.
